title: Headline drop counters shrink 22px → 18px in a PR whose stated purpose is bigger fonts
evidence:
-		noc_col(v, fmt.tprintf("%d", feed.drop_e9), 22, NOC_RED, head_lbl_r + 8, y)
-		noc_col(v, fmt.tprintf("%d", feed.drop_pool), 22, NOC_AMBER, NOC_PANEL_X + NOC_PANEL_W - 6, y)
+		noc_col(v, fmt.tprintf("%d", feed.drop_e9), NOC_SIZE_BODY, NOC_RED, head_lbl_r + 8, y)
+		noc_col(v, fmt.tprintf("%d", feed.drop_pool), NOC_SIZE_BODY, NOC_AMBER, px + NOC_PANEL_W - 6, y)
--- PR body: "KYLE's live-screen assessment: **1.5–2× needed**" ; "| Body / counters | `NOC_SIZE_BODY` | **18px** | 14–15px | +29% |" ; header context: "(2) hierarchy: small-caps labels, large numerals, the drop-reason counters are the headline row"
detail: The DROPS headline numerals were 22px; the new ladder's largest body rung is 18px, so the headline counters got smaller. The PR's old-size table (14–15px) omits the 22px it replaced.
recommended_fix: Add a headline rung (≥22px) to the ladder for the drop counters, or keep 22px for those two numerals; correct the PR's old-size table.

title: del column math contradicts its own comment: 7-digit del counters overlap the 190px name zone
evidence:
+	// the units stay put as counters tick). 18px Plex Mono digit ≈ 10.8px,
+	// so a 7-digit counter needs 76px + 8px breathing per column.
+	name_x := i32(px + 6)
+	del_r := name_x + 196 // name zone (6..196 = 190px) + the 7-digit del column
+	drop_r := del_r + 84
+	loss_r := drop_r + 84
detail: By the diff's own arithmetic a 7-digit del counter right-aligned at name_x+196 starts at ~name_x+120, inside the stated 190px name zone. drop/loss get exclusive 84px columns; del shares the name zone.
recommended_fix: Give del its own 84px column (del_r ≥ name-zone end + 84), or correct the comment to document the real shared/overlapping name+del zone.

title: PR claims "play_w == win_w in the harness" while the same diff sets the rail on in the harness
evidence:
- **Zero golden drift: 48/48 harness green** — T1 hashes + T2 software pixels + replay gate byte-identical (the rail is runtime-gated; the capture path never presses D; play_w == win_w in the harness). The overlay `.t1` sidecars byte-match the blessed goldens (AC3: overlay is stream-neutral).
--- harness/overlay.odin:
+	// DOCK-RIGHT (fit-to-rail): the capture renders the app's D-on playfield
+	// (play_w = win_w - NOC_RAIL_W) so the frame matches the real run.
+	rnd.view_set_rail(&rc.view, true)
detail: harness/overlay.odin explicitly calls view_set_rail(true), so play_w = win_w − NOC_RAIL_W in the overlay-check/overlay-pixels harness paths. The PR's blanket harness claim is false as stated.
recommended_fix: Scope the claim to the T1/T2 golden paths and state that the PP_DEBUG overlay verbs render with the rail on.

title: NOC_PANEL_W_SCALE is declared but never referenced; the 1.4 scale is duplicated as magic 14/10
evidence:
+	NOC_PANEL_W_SCALE :: 1.4            // the panel-width scale (the ruling)
+	NOC_PANEL_W       :: 360 * 14 / 10 // 504 (= 360 × NOC_PANEL_W_SCALE, exact int math) — the rail width
--- test:
+	testing.expect(t, NOC_PANEL_W == 504, "the rail width = 360 x 1.4 = 504")
detail: No code or test reads NOC_PANEL_W_SCALE; the relationship exists only in a comment, and the "pins the scale" test asserts a literal without referencing it.
recommended_fix: Delete the constant, or make the test derive the expected width from NOC_PANEL_W_SCALE so the documented relationship is enforced.

title: NOC_PANEL_MARGIN comment says the rail is inset from the window edge, but the plate is flush against it
detail: rect.x = win_w − NOC_RAIL_W with width NOC_RAIL_W puts the plate's right edge exactly at win_w — no inset. Only the content column is inset; the comment describes the wrong element.
recommended_fix: Reword the comment: the margin insets the content column from the window edge; the plate runs flush to the edge.

title: PR's "mechanically verified" coordinates contradict the shipped constants (plate 757 vs 756, row y 120 vs 116)
evidence:
- e2e OFF frame: zero rail pixels (no D → no panel). Fit-to-rail mechanically verified: world's right edge at x=755, plate at x=757, content first row at y=120.
--- code:
+NOC_CONTENT_Y     :: 116            // the first content row's y (below the top band)
+	return {f32(win_w - NOC_RAIL_W), 0, f32(NOC_RAIL_W), f32(win_h)}
detail: At 1280 wide the code puts the plate's left edge at 1280−524 = 756 (not 757) and row 0 at y=116 (not 120). The verification numbers don't match the constants they claim to verify.
recommended_fix: Re-measure and correct the PR numbers, or align the constants with the measured geometry — at least one side is wrong.
